exam: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
q: What is the percentage of sharing of assistance between central and state governments (in that order) under the Prime Minister Awaas Yojana (gramin)?
explanation:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (60 : 40); it is added as option 5.
PMAY-G cost is shared 60:40 between the Centre and States in plain areas, 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States and 100% central for UTs without legislature; none of the printed ratios (80:20, 75:25, 70:30, 90:10) is the general share. (Printed: no key.)

exam: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
q: Who constructs the house under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana?
explanation: Under PMAY-G the beneficiary constructs the house (with technical support), not a contractor, committee or the government.

q: Real time evidence based progress house construction under PMAY (Gramin) is done through?
explanation: AwaasApp lets beneficiaries upload geo-tagged, time-stamped photos for real-time, evidence-based monitoring of PMAY-G houses.

q: The Indira Awas Yojana program was restructured into PMAY (Gramin) with effect from?
explanation: Indira Awaas Yojana was restructured into PMAY-Gramin with effect from 1 April 2016.

notes.text: - **Indira Awaas Yojana** (began **1985**, independent **1996**) was **restructured into PMAY-G with effect from 1 April 2016** – to **address the gaps** in IAY (poor targeting, small units, weak monitoring), not because of its name.

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
q: Why the IAY program was restructured as PMAY (Gramin)
options: As a policy not to name schemes after individuals
The progam was not known to all
To address gaps in the program
key_text: To address gaps in the program
explanation: IAY was restructured as PMAY-G to address gaps in the programme (poor targeting, small units, weak monitoring and quality), not as a naming policy.
